local_checks.invariant: The changed tests still fail a quadratic regression of the secret scan and still cap a hang, so the guard does not become weaker than the fixed bound it replaces
local_checks.result: scripts/ is unchanged against d2389a05; the scanner under test (secret_findings :2210, mask_json_strings :2278, validate_no_obvious_secrets :2542) is the same. linear_growth (tests/unit/test_validate_agent_assets.py:171-205) times scan(0), a reference at the shorter size, scan(1) and a reference at the longer size in turn, five times, and keeps the least of each. The reference is re.findall of one character over the same text, repeated a calibrated constant number of rounds at both sizes, so its growth over the step is the size factor, 8x. LinearGrowth.judged (:155-160) divides the scan's growth by the reference's. Over the 8x step a linear scan judges about 1 and a quadratic one about 8 (64x over 8x), against the bound 3 (:2881, :3023; asserted at :2921-2926 and :3049-3050); a quadratic scan would pass only if the linear reference grew 21x or more over the step. In units of the size factor the old bound (24 on the raw ratio, about 3x linear) and the new one (3x the reference) have the same nominal sensitivity, and the new one cancels load that hits the pair alike. The 20 s hang cap still applies to both judged sizes (:2918-2920, :3041-3042). The 2,000 size of the padded-line test keeps its correctness assertions and is no longer timed (:2894-2906), as its docstring states. Correctness assertions on every size and form are unchanged. One dilution is new: the one-finding-per-line test now times the fixture write inside scan (:3029-3035), a linear cost that can hide part of a quadratic term when the write dominates the 8,000-finding scan (hardening note).

hardening_notes: tests/unit/test_validate_agent_assets.py:3029-3035 times path.write_text inside the scan that linear_growth judges; the old test wrote the fixture outside the timed region. A linear write that costs several times the report scan at 8,000 findings would dilute a quadratic report below the bound of 3 (for a write four times the scan, a fully quadratic report judges about 2.4). Timing only validate_no_obvious_secrets, or asserting the write's share, would keep the guard's full sensitivity.

The reference's round count is calibrated from one timed call of scan(0) and one of the reference (:193), the first calls of the test; a cold first call inflates it, which changes only the reference's absolute time, not its growth ratio, so the judged value is unaffected.
